claim: Rise/fall matching (trise/tfall within 0.9-1.1, per line and across the pair) and output signal crossover voltage (1.3-2.0 V) of the sky130 FS line driver into the 50 pF test load under local device mismatch (Monte Carlo, vary=mismatch, `*_mm` library sections), at tt (27 C, 3.3 V) and at the corners of the 45-point record sim/driver-signal-quality/records/20261009-182102-e232b2f.md where each row has the thinnest deterministic margin: fs / 100 C / 3.6 V (crossover max 1.9933 V), sf / -40 C / 3.6 V (matching ratio max 1.0772) and fs / 100 C / 3.0 V (matching ratio min 0.9278), against spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 rows 'Rise/fall time' (matching part) and 'Output signal crossover voltage'. Schematic-level, no layout parasitics; not a signoff or catalog-tier claim.

corners.basis: thinnest crossover margin of the 45-point record sim/driver-signal-quality/records/20261009-182102-e232b2f.md: vcross_rise_v 1.9933 V and vcross_fall_v 1.99318 V at fs / 100 C / 3.60 V against the 2.0 V limit
thinnest high-side matching margin of the same record: trf_dp_ratio 1.0772 (trf_x2_ratio 1.07719, trf_dm_ratio 1.07714) at sf / -40 C / 3.60 V against the 1.1 limit
thinnest low-side matching margin of the same record: trf_dm_ratio 0.927808 (trf_x1_ratio 0.927808, trf_dp_ratio 0.927857) at fs / 100 C / 3.00 V against the 0.9 limit

vcross_rise_v.spice: .meas tran vcross_rise_v FIND v(dp) WHEN v(dp)=v(dm) RISE=1

vcross_fall_v.spice: .meas tran vcross_fall_v FIND v(dp) WHEN v(dp)=v(dm) FALL=1

control.description: fixed 180 ohm load from each line to ground (deterministic: collapses the high level, pulling both crossings below 1.3 V) via the testbench rload_ohm parameter

record.netlist_provenance: schematic-derived netlist: xschem export of design/differential_driver.sch (design/netlist/differential_driver.spice) plus the Monte Carlo testbench deck, frozen per campaign; no layout, no parasitic extraction
record.statistical_convention: Monte Carlo of local device mismatch only (monte_carlo.vary = mismatch): n = 400 samples per corner, base seed 166, per-sample seeds derived by `klt sim` (seed contract: sim.md 'Monte Carlo sampling'); every MOS instance of the driver draws independent mismatch (mc_mm_switch = 1 through the `*_mm` library sections); the driver has no resistor or capacitor of its own, and global process spread is the separate corner axis (the corners named here plus the 45- and 225-point deterministic records) and is not sampled
method: Stimulus and measurements as instance xa of sim/driver-signal-quality: DRVEN = OE = 1, TXDP = ctl, TXDM = not ctl, ctl rises at 100 ns and falls at 200 ns with 0.5 ns edges, 50 pF from each line to ground, window 0-300 ns at 20 ps; the corner supply, temperature and `*_mm` library section come from the request. Enable/disable instances are not included.

Matching: `trf_dp_ratio` = trise_dp/tfall_dp, `trf_dm_ratio` = trise_dm/tfall_dm, and across the pair `trf_x1_ratio` = trise_dp/tfall_dm, `trf_x2_ratio` = trise_dm/tfall_dp (10 %-90 % of the corner supply), each required inside 0.9-1.1 as in the deterministic record. Crossover: `vcross_rise_v` / `vcross_fall_v` = v(dp) at v(dp) = v(dm) on the rising / falling transition, required inside 1.3-2.0 V. A sample whose measurement cannot be taken is reported by klt yield as `errored`; the lint requires errored = 0 for a PASS record.

Crossover is graded because the deterministic record leaves it 7 mV of margin at fs / 100 C / 3.60 V (1.9933 V against 2.0 V), so it is mismatch-limited; the rise/fall time row itself (4-20 ns) is global-spread-limited and is not graded here.

Each (receiver, corner) is its own population (one `klt sim` Monte Carlo request, backend batch, per corner); nothing is pooled across corners. `klt yield-samples` pairs each nominal campaign with its negative-control campaign (same deck, same seeds, the deterministic asymmetry below), and `klt yield` grades the pair against the row limits with target_yield 0.99 at 95 % confidence.

Negative control (deterministic), one per receiver because the two rows fail in different ways: for `match` a fixed 330 ohm load from each line to ground (slows every rising edge and speeds every falling edge, so all four ratios rise to about 1.5, far above 1.1); for `xover` a fixed 180 ohm load from each line to ground (the high level collapses and both crossings fall to about 1.26 V, below 1.3 V; at that load the 90 % level is never reached, so the ratios could not be measured and `xover` carries the crossover measurements only). The yield report must flag every graded measurement `detected`; a campaign whose control is `not_detected` cannot be a PASS record. The two receivers share one nominal deck and seeds, so their nominal samples are identical; they are separate campaigns only so that each row has a control that actually degrades it.

Mismatch activity: the per-sample spread (stddev in each yield report's `distribution`) of the ratios and crossover voltages is the evidence that mismatch reached the g5v0d10v5 devices (a stddev of zero would fail the record).
PDK: the pinned open_pdks revision of sim/pdk-pins.json (current pin); each record states the revision and the model library sha256.
record.footer: Scope: schematic-level statistical evidence for one block against the ratified rise/fall matching and crossover-voltage rows, at the corners named in the record. Local device mismatch only; global process spread is covered by the deterministic corner records, and the corner x mismatch combination is limited to the corners named. It does not claim the rise/fall time (4-20 ns) range under mismatch, layout, DRC/LVS or signoff, and does not relax any target. A FAIL record is evidence of failure, not compliance.

yield.sample_size_justification: target_yield 0.99 at 95 % two-sided confidence: with zero observed failures the exact (Clopper-Pearson) lower bound reaches 0.99 only for n >= 368 (klt yield `required_n_for_target`), so n = 400 per corner is the smallest round count that can support the claim; the +/-0.01 precision target needs n >= 183. A failing row is not rescued by a larger n: it is recorded as failing.
